description: Make CORS allowed origins configurable via CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated) in routes/router.go, defaulting to * when empty so dev is unchanged. Reflect the request Origin when it matches the list. Document the env in .env.example. Independent of other features; touches routes/router.go and .env.example.
steps: In routes/router.go, inside NewRouter and BEFORE the CORS middleware is registered, read and parse the allowlist once: `raw := os.Getenv("CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS")`; split on ',' and strings.TrimSpace each, dropping empties, into a []string allowed. Add imports `os` and `strings`.

Rewrite the inline CORS middleware: if len(allowed) == 0, keep current behavior -> set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to "*". Otherwise read the request Origin header; if it is in `allowed`, set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to that exact origin; else set it to allowed[0] (deterministic fallback). Keep the existing Access-Control-Allow-Methods, Access-Control-Allow-Headers, Access-Control-Max-Age headers and the OPTIONS short-circuit (w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK); return) exactly as today.
Add CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to .env.example with a comment explaining: comma-separated list of allowed origins; leave empty to allow all (*) in development.
acceptance_criteria: routes/router.go reads CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and defaults to "*" when empty (dev behavior preserved).
When the env lists origins, a matching request Origin is reflected in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; a non-matching origin does not receive "*".
The OPTIONS preflight short-circuit and the other CORS headers are preserved.
The Docker gate command passes: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
verification: docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app golang:1.22-bullseye sh -c "go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./..." — all pass.
findings: Implemented in routes/router.go: parse CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS once (comma-separated, TrimSpace each, drop empties) before registering the CORS middleware. When the list is empty, Access-Control-Allow-Origin stays "*" so dev behavior is unchanged. When origins are configured, the request Origin header is reflected if it matches the allowlist, otherwise it falls back to allowed[0] (deterministic, never "*"). The Access-Control-Allow-Methods/Headers/Max-Age headers and the OPTIONS preflight short-circuit are preserved exactly. Added os and strings imports. Documented CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS in .env.example (comma-separated; empty allows all in dev). Docker gate passed: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... all succeeded (config, controllers, helpers tests ok; no test regressions).
